questions.prompt: A relay's coil is energized. What does a **normally closed** contact of that relay do?
options: Nothing: only normally open contacts change
It closes for one scan, then opens
questions.explanation: "Normally" means with the coil off. Energize the coil and every contact changes over: a normally closed contact opens.

questions.prompt: Match each ladder symbol to what it is.
questions.explanation: Contacts read a tag (or a relay's state); the coil at the right-hand end of the rung sets one.

questions.prompt: Fill in the seal-in rung's result. Remember that Stop is TRUE while nobody presses it.
questions.explanation: The motor runs when Start is pressed or it is already running (the seal-in), and Stop is not pressed (TRUE).

questions.prompt: Why is a Stop button wired **normally closed**?
options: So a broken wire stops the machine, as if Stop were pressed
Because a PLC can only read closed contacts
So the program can check it with a normally closed contact
questions.explanation: A broken wire makes the input FALSE, the same as pressing Stop: the machine fails safe.

questions.prompt: A door motor has an Up contactor and a Down contactor. Which of these are **interlocks**? Choose every one that is.
options: A normally closed contact of Down in the Up rung
A normally closed contact of Up in the Down rung
Up's own contact in parallel with the Open button
A limit switch at the top of the travel
questions.explanation: An interlock locks one output out while the other is on. Up's own contact is the seal-in, and the limit switch stops the travel.

questions.prompt: A contactor coil rated 24 V DC has a resistance of 240 Ω. How much current does it draw, in milliamps?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law: I = V / R = 24 V / 240 Ω = 0.1 A, which is 100 mA.
